mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-on-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 15% signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both unemployment rate and payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a paradoxical labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower unemployment, suggesting structural issues that depress consumer confidence and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises while PAYEMS also rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 40% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals reduced household buffer and constrained consumption, which lowers corporate revenue expectations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.
